Group homomorphisms

Source: R/combinatorics-fpgroups.R
GroupHomomorphism.Rd

homomorphism(domain, codomain, gens, images) is the homomorphism that maps the generators gens of domain to images (the other generators go to the identity); domain and codomain are permutation groups, finitely presented groups or free groups. With check = TRUE the images are checked against the relators of the domain (the presentation of a permutation group). Between permutation groups the result is the package's GroupHomomorphism; otherwise it is an FpGroupHomomorphism. hom_is_injective(), hom_is_surjective(), hom_is_isomorphism() and hom_is_trivial() test properties of either kind, hom_images() gives the images of the generators (SymPy's images dictionary), hom_compose(T, S) is T after S, hom_factor() gives a surjection and an injection whose composite is T, hom_restrict_to() restricts to a subgroup and hom_invert_subgroup() gives a preimage subgroup. group_isomorphism() searches an isomorphism and is_isomorphic() tests for one. Applying, inverting, kernels and images are hom_apply(), hom_invert(), hom_kernel() and hom_image().

Usage

GroupHomomorphism(domain, codomain, images)

hom_images(T)

hom_is_injective(T)

hom_is_surjective(T)

hom_is_isomorphism(T)

hom_is_trivial(T)

hom_factor(T)

hom_compose(T, other)

hom_restrict_to(T, H)

hom_invert_subgroup(T, H)

homomorphism(domain, codomain, gens, images = list(), check = TRUE)

group_isomorphism(G, H, isomorphism = TRUE)

is_isomorphic(G, H)

Arguments

domain, codomain, G, H

Groups.

images

A list of elements of the codomain; for GroupHomomorphism() an ordered dictionary as built by homomorphism().

T, other

Homomorphisms.

gens

A list of generators of the domain.

check

Check that the images define a homomorphism.

isomorphism

Also return the isomorphism.

Value

A homomorphism (an environment), a group or a logical.

Examples

g <- free_group("a, b")
a <- g[[2]]; b <- g[[3]]
G <- FpGroup(g[[1]], list(a^3, b^3, (a * b)^2))
A <- AlternatingGroup(4)
T <- homomorphism(G, A, list(a, b), list(Permutation(0, 1, 2, size = 4), Permutation(1, 2, 3)))
hom_is_isomorphism(T)
#> [1] TRUE
is_isomorphic(G, A)
#> [1] TRUE
